candidates.attacker_control: Any value an application/HTL template passes to XSSAPI.getValidHref() from untrusted input: e.g. an HTL binding in an href/src attribute is routed through XSSRuntimeExtension.applyXSSFilter (bundles/scripting/sightly/engine/src/main/java/org/apache/sling/scripting/sightly/impl/engine/extension/XSSRuntimeExtension.java lines 108-109 and 145-150, where 'src'/'href' attribute contexts are mapped to MarkupContext.URI), or direct use of XSSAPI by Sling components/applications, or stored values (link fields) later rendered as hrefs.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Plain `javascript:` schemes are blocked by the allow-list (colon not permitted); offsite URLs are restricted to http(s)/ftp/mailto. getValidHref also encodes quotes/angle brackets, so attribute-breakout payloads are handled. The bypass depends on HTML character-reference decoding by the browser, which is standard for attribute values, and on the value not being passed through an additional HTML-attribute encoder (HTL's URI context returns getValidHref output verbatim, so this holds in-repo). The shipped policy (config.xml lines 244-249) and the hardcoded fallback DEFAULT_HREF_ATTRIBUTE (XSSFilterImpl lines 58-66) contain identical regexps, so both policy-present and fallback paths are affected. I could not confirm the upstream CVE/fix mapping offline, and no test was executed.
candidates.impact: Cross-site scripting in pages protected by the Sling XSS Protection API (including default HTL href/src contexts), allowing script execution in a victim's authenticated session: cookie/session data theft, page/UI manipulation, and state-changing requests in the Sling application. Because the vulnerable method is Sling's designated URL validator, applications that follow the documented contract (XSSAPI.java lines 92-99: 'Sanitizes a URL for writing as an HTML href or src attribute value') do not add further encoding.
candidates.prerequisites: Attacker-controlled string reaches XSSAPI.getValidHref (HTL href/src binding or an application using the XSS API); payload contains only characters allowed by the href regexps — e.g. `javascript:alert(1)` (no quotes/spaces needed); the returned value is placed in an HTML attribute context without additional HTML-attribute encoding; a victim views the page and clicks the link for script execution.
candidates.root_cause: XSSAPI.getValidHref() (XSSAPIImpl) only percent-encodes quotes, angle brackets, backtick and spaces, then delegates to XSSFilter.isValidHref(). XSSFilterImpl.isValidHref() (a) lowercases and checks the raw, non-canonicalized string against AntiSamy allowed values (empty list) and (b) full-matches it against the policy href regexps — or, when the policy defines no href, the hardcoded DEFAULT_HREF_ATTRIBUTE with the same expressions (onsiteURL `([\p{L}\p{N}\\.\#@\$%\+&;\-_~,\?=/!\*\(\)]*|\#(\w)+)`, offsiteURL limited to http/ftp/mailto). Because '&', '#', ';' and digits are allowed, HTML character references survive validation; downstream HTML parsers decode them in attribute values. The in-code comment 'Same logic as in MagicSAXFilter.startElement()' is invalid here: AntiSamy's SAX filter receives entity-decoded attribute values, whereas this validator receives the raw string, so no canonicalization/entity decoding occurs before the scheme check.
candidates.title: XSS Protection API href validation bypass via HTML character references (getValidHref/isValidHref)
candidates.trace: 1) Input `javascript:alert(1)` enters XSSAPIImpl.getValidHref (lines 212-222): only `"`, `'`, `>`, `<`, backtick and space are percent-encoded, so `&`, `#`, `5`, `8`, `;` remain. 2) XSSFilterImpl.isValidHref (lines 244-250): containsAllowedValue() is false (empty allowed-values list), then matchesAllowedExpression() full-matches the raw string against the onsiteURL regexp; every character (letters, digits, '&', '#', ';', '(', ')') is in the allowed class, so it returns true. 3) getValidHref returns the string unchanged (line 230) as 'safe for href/src'. 4) When rendered as `<a href="javascript:alert(1)">`, the browser decodes the character reference `:` to ':', yielding the actionable scheme `javascript:alert(1)`; a click executes script in the page origin. 5) Counter-check: a plain `javascript:alert(1)` payload is correctly rejected (':' is not in the allow-list and the offsite regexp only allows http(s)/ftp/mailto), and percent-encoded/whitespace variants are not matched — the bypass specifically exploits the absence of entity decoding before validation.
candidates.unverified: Exact upstream CVE identifier/fix commit (e.g. CVE-2017-15717 vs CVE-2017-15718) and whether the upstream fix canonicalized the URL in XSSFilterImpl, changed getValidHref, or altered the shipped policy — not verifiable without external data. Runtime exploitability was not executed; the reasoning relies on AntiSamy 1.5.2 Attribute.matchesAllowedExpression() full-match semantics (pattern.matcher(value).matches()) and standard HTML character-reference decoding. An orphaned test resource (bundles/extensions/xss/src/test/resources/configWithoutHref.xml, referenced by no source file) suggests test activity around XSSFilterImpl href validation but is only a navigation hint.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS) — sanitizer/validator bypass

coverage_summary: Scope: get_source_scope reports 6311 source-root files, 6310 model-visible (1 excluded by sensitive-name-or-path filter, 0 symlinks, 0 files over 5 MiB); binary-like files are refused/skipped. get_relation_scope reports a partial index authored over 6310 files / 4910 Java files with 718 omitted files, 7 parse errors, 56017 symbols and no control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution, Spring runtime, or reachability support; index edges are syntactic navigation candidates only and were all re-verified against source text. I concentrated on security-relevant areas: org.apache.sling.xss (XSSAPI/Filter/policy, tested against the shipped AntiSamy policy and the hardcoded default), auth core/form (redirect validation and login flows), engine and servlet resolver error handling, servlets/get and servlets/post, jcr contentloader/webdav, resourceresolver mapping, fsresource/fsclassloader, scripting/sightly XSS runtime, and commons modules. The snapshot corresponds to Apache Sling trunk circa mid/late 2017 (parent 29-SNAPSHOT, provisioning lists Oak 1.5.5, xss 1.0.11-SNAPSHOT, servlets.post 2.3.13-SNAPSHOT), so findings were assessed against the security APIs of that revision. This was not an exhaustive line-by-line review of all 6310 files.
limitations: No code was executed and no tests/scanners were run; the candidate is a static-reasoning lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.
The exact VUL4J-24 CVE/fix mapping could not be verified offline; the xss module identification rests on module versions, the security API contract, and an orphaned href-policy test resource.

AntiSamy 1.5.2 library internals (Attribute.containsAllowedValue/matchesAllowedExpression) were reasoned from their documented/expected behavior and the in-repo policy regexps, not from library source present in the snapshot (antisamy is an external dependency).
The P1 relation index is partial (718 omitted files, 7 parse errors) and provides no data/control flow or reachability proof, so unreported code areas may contain issues not seen here.

One file was excluded by the run's sensitive-name-or-path filter and could not be inspected; it may be relevant to the xss test suite (e.g. a missing test class for the orphaned configWithoutHref.xml resource).

Browser-side entity decoding in href attributes and the absence of additional HTML-attribute encoding by consumers were assumed from the in-repo HTL integration (XSSRuntimeExtension) and standard HTML semantics; they were not exercised at runtime.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE-style parsing in XSSAPIImpl.getValidXML (bundles/extensions/xss/src/main/java/org/apache/sling/xss/impl/XSSAPIImpl.java lines 62-68 and 370-389): SAXParserFactory is created with only setValidating(false)/setNamespaceAware(true), so DOCTYPE/external entities are not disabled and an attacker-supplied XML string can trigger external entity resolution (SSRF/local-file read/DoS).
rejected_leads.reason: Strong code evidence but no in-repo callers of getValidXML, so impact depends entirely on downstream application usage; a unit-testable failing behavior is less clear, and I could not determine whether this maps to VUL4J-24. Left as an unconfirmed alternative in the same module/file.

rejected_leads.lead: Open redirect via backslashes in AuthUtil.isRedirectValid (bundles/auth/core/src/main/java/org/apache/sling/auth/core/AuthUtil.java lines 451-508): the method rejects '//', '/../', '/./' but not '\', so with an empty context path a target such as '/\evil.com' is considered valid and is passed to sendRedirect (callers include SlingAuthenticator.redirectAfterLogout line 1429, DefaultAuthenticationFeedbackHandler line 79, FormAuthenticationHandler line 508); browsers normalize '\' to '/' making '//evil.com' protocol-relative.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible code weakness but impact is limited to open redirect/phishing (no script execution), and there is no benchmark signal pointing to auth/core; a stricter source-evidence/threat-mapping bar is met less clearly than the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Reflected XSS in FSClassLoaderWebConsole.renderContent (bundles/commons/fsclassloader/src/main/java/org/apache/sling/commons/fsclassloader/impl/FSClassLoaderWebConsole.java lines 376-398): the 'view' parameter is concatenated into the HTML output ('Viewing Script: ' + root + file) without escaping.
rejected_leads.reason: The plugin is an admin-authenticated Felix Web Console servlet, and isValid() restricts the reflected value to an existing file below the class-loader root, greatly limiting injectable characters; no CVE association found.

rejected_leads.lead: URL resolution / potential SSRF in JCR content loader XmlReader (bundles/jcr/contentloader/src/main/java/org/apache/sling/jcr/contentloader/internal/readers/XmlReader.java lines 359, 563-576): xml-stylesheet href and nt:file src are resolved as URLs and fetched (TransformerFactory/URL.openStream).
rejected_leads.reason: parse(URL) is only invoked from BundleContentLoader (bundle-provided, trusted content); the attacker-reachable POST :operation=import path calls parse(InputStream) with a null xmlLocation, which disables both processing instructions and nt:file handling, so no untrusted path to the sinks was confirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: Open redirect via SlingPostServlet :redirect handling (bundles/servlets/post/src/main/java/org/apache/sling/servlets/post/impl/SlingPostServlet.java lines 235-361).
rejected_leads.reason: getRedirectUrl already rejects URIs with an authority component (lines 312-317), and the scheme-pattern branch is effectively unreachable for absolute external URLs; no second bypass beyond the generic backslash issue was demonstrated.

summary: Reviewed the Apache Sling trunk snapshot (builder 9-SNAPSHOT, parent 29-SNAPSHOT, Oak 1.5.5 — circa mid/late 2017). The strongest source-evidenced candidate is an XSS-protection bypass in the org.apache.sling.xss bundle: XSSAPI.getValidHref() returns a value that XSSFilterImpl.isValidHref() has validated, but that validation matches the raw, non-canonicalized string against AntiSamy href allow-list regexps that permit '&', '#', ';' and digits. An HTML-character-reference payload such as `javascript:alert(1)` therefore passes validation and is returned unchanged; when the value is written into an href/src attribute (e.g. HTL URI context, which calls getValidHref directly), the browser decodes `:` back to ':' and the link becomes `javascript:alert(1)`. Other plausible issues (XXE-style parsing in getValidXML, backslash open-redirect in AuthUtil, admin-console XSS in FSClassLoaderWebConsole, content-loader URL resolution) were evaluated and are weaker or less reachable; none was submitted as an additional candidate.
